# Workspace releases

The root `pi-roundtable` package and every `packages/*` workspace share one version.
Drawing, coding, web, sandbox, and MCP live here with their full original Git history; webchat, line and browser started here.
A single `v<version>` tag runs `publish.yml`: the existing core job checks the entire tree and publishes the core, then a matrix publishes each workspace independently.
The matrix is generated by `scripts/check-release.ts` and includes all eight workspaces.
The root's `files` allowlist does not include `packages/`.

## Development

Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` at the repository root.
After changing workspace manifests, remove root and workspace `node_modules` before installing: Bun's incremental relinking can leave child-local core links pointing at the child itself (seen with Bun 1.4.2).
The workspace linkage regression test fails on such stale links.
If they persist after a clean install, rebuild `bun.lock` from scratch with the Bun version CI pins (`bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and review the newly resolved dependencies: its older lockfile format can retain invalid nested root entries.
The committed lockfile uses the current format; clean installation and repeated frozen installation both pass the linkage regression.
Bun does not treat the root package as a child workspace; the root-only `pi-roundtable: link:.` override and hoisted linker give every workspace a live symlink to the core.
Workspace manifests use ordinary semver for both the core development dependency and its peer range.
No workspace or local-path dependency specifier is shipped in a workspace manifest.
A consuming project ignores the root package's development override.

Run core checks with `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run test`.
Run all workspace checks with `bun run check:packages`.
Run `bun run --cwd packages/web build` to build the console assets.
CI performs these checks with PostgreSQL and native canvas prerequisites installed, including MCP's PostgreSQL tests.
Sandbox's Docker integration is opt-in locally; CI explicitly enables it on the native Linux Ubuntu runner with its local Docker daemon and non-root runner account:

```sh
(cd packages/sandbox && SANDBOX_DOCKER_TEST=1 bun test src/docker.integration.test.ts)
```

CI and the core publication gate both run this test and require the native Linux, non-root, opt-in conditions rather than accepting a skipped test.
The test keeps the production isolation flags and credential broker intact.
Docker Desktop on macOS is not an execution substitute because it does not share host Unix sockets into Linux containers.

## First publication and trust

These are owner actions, not part of a routine release.
Use Node 24 and npm 11.15 or newer, enable account 2FA, and log in with browser/security-key authentication using `npm login`.
Run `npm login --auth-type=web && npm whoami` before a manual publication: a logged-out `npm publish` fails with a misleading `E404 PUT Not found`.
All eight workspaces are on npm (version 0.22.5 when this was written) and trust this repository's `publish.yml`, so a tag publishes every one of them with provenance.
The steps below apply only when a new workspace is added.

### A new workspace's first publication

The package must exist on npm before trusted publishing can be configured, so the first lockstep tag that includes a new workspace stops at preflight until the owner publishes it once by hand, from the release commit after its CI passes.
From the repository root, with the checks above passing:

```sh
(cd packages/<name> && npm publish --access public --provenance=false)
npm trust github pi-roundtable-<name> --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
npm trust list pi-roundtable-<name>
```

Local publication disables provenance because provenance is generated by supported CI environments, not a developer's shell.
Verify the list names this repository and `publish.yml`.
Then `bun scripts/preflight-release.ts v<version>` without `--local` finds the package and passes; push the `v<version>` tag.

What follows, and is expected:

- That version on npm is the hand publication and has no provenance; from the next version on, the tag publishes the package with provenance like every other one.
- The tag's Publish run publishes the core and every other workspace as usual, but its `Publish pi-roundtable-<name>` matrix job fails at `npm publish`: the version already exists, which npm reports as EPUBLISHCONFLICT ("cannot publish over the previously published versions"). `fail-fast: false` keeps the other matrix jobs running, so only that job fails and the run is red.
- Check that job's log: a failure for any other reason, or a failure of another job, is a real failure and is handled as below. Do not rerun that job; it can only fail the same way.

Sandbox and browser ship Docker-backed code.
Their integration tests need a native Linux host with a local Docker daemon and run on CI's Ubuntu runner; CI and the core publication gate both require the native Linux, non-root, opt-in conditions rather than accepting a skipped test:

```sh
(cd packages/browser && BROWSER_DOCKER_TEST=1 bun test src/docker.integration.test.ts)
```

Browser ships its Dockerfile but not an image: a host builds the image once from the installed package (see the package README), so the release publishes no container.

## Subsequent lockstep releases

Before choosing the version, run `git fetch --tags origin` and compare the local tags with `git ls-remote --tags origin` and `npm view pi-roundtable dist-tags`: a checkout behind origin once picked versions that were already published.
Update the root version and every workspace version together.
Update every workspace's core development dependency to that version and its peer range to the matching minor, written `>=<major>.<minor>.0 <<major>.<minor+1>.0` for version `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, such as the range the other workspaces' manifests already carry.
Update changelogs, regenerate `bun.lock`, and run the clean-install checks and packing checks.
The version bump changes the lockfile's workspace entries, so commit `bun.lock` with the bump and confirm `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes locally before pushing.
Run `bun scripts/check-release.ts v<version>` before committing: it refuses mismatched versions, core peer ranges, development pins, and repository directories.
Run `bun scripts/preflight-release.ts v<version>`: it packs every workspace, checks required files (including the web HTML/JS/CSS, drawing fonts, and sandbox worker sources), and requires each package to exist on npm before the core can publish.
Use `--local` only for CI or pre-first-publish checks, where a new package need not yet exist on npm.
Run preflight with the npm that `publish.yml` installs (`npm@latest`), for example from `npm install --prefix <tmp> npm@latest` placed first on `PATH`: npm 12 changed the JSON shape of `npm pack --json` and `npm view --json`, and an older local npm does not exercise it.
If the release adds a workspace, it needs [its first publication](#a-new-workspaces-first-publication) first.
Verify every workspace's trusted publisher is configured against this repository's `publish.yml` before pushing a release tag; package existence alone does not prove OIDC authorization.
Commit and push, wait for CI for that exact commit, then have the owner push the single `v<version>` tag.
`publish.yml` checks all versions before any publication and publishes all packages with provenance through npm OIDC, except a new workspace, as [its first publication](#a-new-workspaces-first-publication) describes.
If a package job fails after other packages publish, rerun only the failed jobs rather than republishing the successful core or packages.
Do not use Re-run all jobs: npm refuses to overwrite the already-published core version, stopping the downstream matrix.
Publication across multiple npm packages is not atomic; pack/existence preflight cannot guarantee registry availability or OIDC authorization.
